name: Saturn from Voyager 2, August 31, 1981
blurb: The ringed planet, about 120,500 kilometers across at the equator. Seen by Voyager 2's wide-angle camera through orange, green, blue and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: The whole of Saturn, partly in shadow, from about 5.4 million kilometers away, 5 days after Voyager 2's closest approach to Saturn on August 26, 1981. Its rings are billions of chunks of ice and rock, from dust-sized grains to pieces as big as a house.
